title: The Love of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The love of God is His holy, faithful, self-giving goodness by which He sets His affection on His people and gives Himself for their good. God’s love is not sentimental weakness; it is pure, covenantal, righteous, and most clearly revealed in Jesus Christ.
summary: The love of God is His holy, faithful, self-giving goodness by which He sets His affection on His people and gives Himself for their good. God’s love is not sentimental weakness; it is pure, covenantal, righteous, and most clearly revealed in Jesus Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the fullest display of God’s love. God shows His love by sending His Son to save sinners, and Christ shows His love by laying down His life for His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s love begins in God Himself. Scripture says God is love, not because love is greater than God, but because love belongs to His eternal character. His love is holy, faithful, wise, and true.

The love of God is not based on human worthiness. Israel was not chosen because they were greater than other nations, and sinners are not saved because they are morally impressive. God sets His love according to His grace, faithfulness, and redemptive purpose.

God’s love is revealed most clearly in Christ. While sinners were still sinners, Christ died for them. Love does not ignore sin, deny judgment, or remove the need for repentance. God’s love saves by giving His Son as the atoning sacrifice for sin.

The love of God also transforms His people. Those loved by God are called to love one another. Christian love is not vague kindness without truth, but sacrificial care shaped by the love God has shown in Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people misunderstand love. Some think God’s love means He approves of everything. Others think their suffering, shame, disability, addiction, rejection, or failure proves they are unloved. Scripture gives a stronger foundation: God’s love is revealed in Christ, not measured by circumstances or human approval.

This doctrine gives deep assurance to the believer. God’s love is not fragile, shallow, or easily exhausted. The same God who loved sinners enough to give His Son is able to keep, correct, restore, discipline, and carry His people in faithful love.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive God’s love through Christ rather than trying to earn it or redefine it. Let His love humble your pride, heal your fear, correct your sin, and teach you to love others sacrificially. When circumstances feel painful or confusing, look to the cross as the clearest display of God’s love.
